# Two logical Vulkan outputs with shared read-only glyph input

`VULKAN_TEXT18_DUAL_DEVICE=1 python -m pytest -c tests/pytest.ini tests/test_text18_dual_device_lab.py`
uses the current software-Vulkan toolchain and existing trusted DejaVuSans.
Static collection is integration-marked and does not import native font libraries.
No font or tool downloads are performed.

A single process constructs outputs A/B simultaneously, each with its own
VkInstance, VkDevice, queue, command resources, descriptor pool/set, coverage
image, active color/velocity/ID attachments, D32 depth and readback/staging buffers.
Actual live VkDevice handles must be different. Physical-device UUIDs are not
compared across VkInstances. This is **two logical devices
using the same configured software Vulkan implementation**, not different hardware GPUs.

Both read the same const CPU glyph masks, generated by real HarfBuzz→FreeType
for O/ffi/Arabic. Missing glyphs/clipping reject; fixed font SHA validates before
parsing. Native CPU inputs are compared with an immutable saved copy after all
draws; Python input files have before/after hashes. No cross-device GPU handles
are shared. Every draw explicitly binds its device's pipeline/descriptors.

Actual sequence:
- A and B independently render O.
- Pause A; its draw guard rejects without frame increment/output. B renders ffi.
- Destroy A. B renders Arabic without recreation.
- Rebuild A at generation1; A renders Arabic and B renders O.
- A renders ffi, waits completion, then a controlled exception destroys A.
  B remains live and renders ffi correctly afterwards.
- B renders O as a legal wrong-input negative against expected ffi, then is destroyed.

Eight positive images plus one negative are real draw/readbacks. Each positive
uses independent fixed mask association and the existing CPU premultiplied oracle
at1e-6. All three color refs are **active**, not UNUSED fallback: fragment shader
emits changed velocity/ID values but per-attachment write masks retain exact
sentinels. D32 ALWAYS/no-write preserves.375 exactly; this tests write protection,
not depth occlusion. Source active-MRT capability queries enable independentBlend.

Events are read from actual object/frame/generation counters and compared with
fixed expected lifecycle. Three devices are created, peak two live, all three
destroyed. Counts measure owned fixture objects, NOT a production/driver memory
leak proof. Paused A has no pending submission. The injected failure is only after
a completed draw; it is not device loss or arbitrary pending/allocation cleanup.
Outer pytest rejects stale B image and forged destruction event on separate copies.
The runner rejects wrong input image and unchanged-output overwrite retry.

Execution is serial on one thread; no parallel scheduling/concurrency claim,
production renderer/window lifecycle, separate physical GPU, target mobile/Windows,
world/shadow second camera, arbitrary state restoration or Live acceptance.
Active-MRT preparation's independent tests are not counted as dual-device evidence.
Subprocesses120s, outer pytest180s, inherited bounded submissions; raw source,
provider, tool, validation/driver hashes and environment details stay local.
